newsitem.title: USA: TCI Comms dives again in US corporate bond trade.
newsitem.headline: TCI Comms dives again in US corporate bond trade.

text.p: TCI Communications, was once again the focus of investment grade corporate bond trading, dealers said, as it lost ground into the close.
Junk bonds faded 1/2 point on average as they continue to consolidate powerful gains seen since July, traders said.

TCI debt was hit early after a Wall Street Journal article highlighted news TCI has told suppliers to stop shipments until further notice, traders said. Prices bounced sharply higher after TCI said it expected to post Q3 revenues of $1.65 billion and operating cash flow of $591 million, traders said, but quickly faded below Wednesday's closing levels.
"Earnings looked okay so there was a relief trade, bonds traded up, and then people realized it was stuff S&P already knew and S&P put them on watch for downgrade," a trader said.
Concerns of high cash flow to debt ratio prompted Standard & Poor's rating agency to submit a negative outlook late last week. If cut, TCI's S&P rating would enter junk bond status.

TCI's 7-7/8 percent debt due 2026 traded as wide as 285 basis points over the Treasury curve in early trade. The debt rebounded to a spread of 265 after the TCI announcement but was quoted at 280 near the close, five to 10 basis points wider on the day.
Shares of TCI fell 1/2 point to 11-5/8, a 52-week low.

Other high-grades spreads were flat to firmer in the broad market, meanwhile. ABN AMRO's $500 million five-year debt offering, priced at 40 basis points over the Treasury curve on Wednesday, traded at issue bid on Thursday, one trader said.

Turning to high-yielders, Stratosphere Corp's 14.25 percent first mortgage notes dropped more than five points in spotty trade after the hotel/casino said it does not plan to make the November 15 interest payment, according to traders.
Stratosphere also said it will likely file bankruptcy in its efforts to restructure the terms of the notes.
